prompt:
Work only from this primary source. For each of the 12 B001 comparisons, determine whether the relevant side of the comparison is actually present in this source:

1. Romans 4:3 / Genesis 15:6
2. Romans 9:25 / Hosea 2:23
3. Romans 9:26 / Hosea 1:10
4. Romans 10:11 / Isaiah 28:16
5. Romans 10:13 / Joel 2:32
6. Romans 11:34 / Isaiah 40:13
7. Romans 15:12 / Isaiah 11:10
8. 1 Corinthians 1:19 / Isaiah 29:14
9. 1 Corinthians 6:16 / Genesis 2:24
10. 1 Corinthians 9:9 / Deuteronomy 25:4
11. 1 Corinthians 10:7 / Exodus 32:6
12. Galatians 3:13 / Deuteronomy 21:23

For a Septuagint/Old Greek edition, extract the relevant Greek Jewish-scriptural wording.

For each B001 ID return:
- status: TEXT_PRESENT / NOT_IN_SOURCE;
- exact passage/reference represented in this source;
- exact printed text needed for comparison;
- printed page or stable locator;
- whether an apparatus entry occurs at the target wording;
- exact apparatus information if present;
- what the apparatus entry does and does not establish.

Do not classify a verse as NOT DISCUSSED merely because the edition has no commentary. The printed text itself is the evidence.

expand_more
In Henry Barclay Swete’s edition of the Septuagint (Volume III: Hosea—4 Maccabees, Cambridge, 1894), the scope of the volume covers the Minor Prophets, the Major Prophets, and the remaining books through 4 Maccabees
1
2
. Consequently, the seven prophetic citations (Hosea, Joel, Isaiah) are TEXT_PRESENT, while the five Pentateuchal citations (Genesis, Exodus, Deuteronomy) belong to Volume I and are NOT_IN_SOURCE
1
2
.
Below is the determination, exact Greek text, printed page locators, and apparatus analysis for each of the twelve B001 comparisons based strictly on this volume.

status: TEXT_PRESENT

καὶ σπερῶ αὐτὴν ἐμαυτῷ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἀγαπήσω τὴν Οὐκ ἠγαπημένην, καὶ ἐρῶ τῷ Οὐ λαῷ μου Λαός μου εἶ σύ, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐρεῖ Κύριος ὁ θεός μου εἶ σύ.

exact apparatus information if present:
23 αγαπησω] ελεησω AQ | ηγαπημενην] ηλεημενην AQ
3
what the apparatus entry does and does not establish:
Does establish: In the base text (Codex Vaticanus, B), the verbs and participles read ἀγαπήσω and ἠγαπημένην, matching the vocabulary of Paul's citation in Romans 9:25 (τὴν οὐκ ἠγαπημένην ἠγαπημένην)
3
. However, Codex Alexandrinus (A) and Codex Marchalianus (Q) read ἐλεήσω and ἠλεημένην, aligning instead with the name Lo-ruhamah in Hosea 1:6, 8 (Οὐκ ἠλεημένη)
3
4
.
Does not establish: Any Greek manuscript support for Paul's exact introductory clause Καλέσω τὸν οὐ λαόν μου λαόν μου; the uncial Septuagint text reads καὶ ἐρῶ τῷ Οὐ λαῷ μου Λαός μου εἶ σύ

καὶ ἦν ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ ὡς ἡ ἄμμος τῆς θαλάσσης, ἣ οὐκ ἐκμετρηθήσεται οὐδὲ ἐξαριθμηθήσεται· καὶ ἔσται ἐν τῷ τόπῳ οὗ ἐρρέθη αὐτοῖς Οὐ λαός μου ὑμεῖς, κληθήσονται καὶ αὐτοὶ υἱοὶ θεοῦ ζῶντος.

Does establish:
Codex Alexandrinus (A) prefixes ἐκεῖ before κληθήσονται (pr εκει A) and omits καὶ αὐτοί (om και αυτοι A)

. This gives the exact reading ἐκεῖ κληθήσονται υἱοὶ θεοῦ ζῶντος, identical to Paul's quotation in Romans 9:26

Symmachus and Theodotion in the margin of Q (Qmg) likewise omit τὸ καί

what the apparatus entry does and does not establish:
Does establish:
While the base text (Codex Vaticanus, B) reads simply καὶ ὁ πιστεύων οὐ μὴ καταισχυνθῇ, Codex Sinaiticus (א), Codex Alexandrinus (A), and Codex Marchalianus (Q) all add ἐπʼ αὐτῷ (+ επ αυτω אAQ)

The Three (Aquila, Symmachus, Theodotion) read οὐ σπεύσει in Qmg, reflecting the Masoretic sense

Does not establish: Any manuscript authority for the universal quantifier Πᾶς prefixed by Paul in Romans 10:11 (Πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων), nor for Paul's future indicative form καταισχυνθήσεται in place of the subjunctive καταισχυνθῇ
